did_you_know.text: The verb “vayosef” can introduce an additional action, not necessarily one that happened immediately after the previous event. Biblical narrative order is not always a complete timeline.
Midian’s descendants later appear in the Bible as the Midianites. For example, Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, is called a priest of Midian.
Isaac and Ishmael bury their father together, even though the Bible previously described tensions between them. This may suggest family cooperation at an important moment.
Beer-lahai-roi is first mentioned as the place where Hagar encountered the angel of the Lord. It is generally associated with the Negev, though its exact location is unknown.
Genesis 17:20 already promised that Ishmael would father twelve princes. Here, that promise appears as an organized list of names and clan leaders.
Paddan-aram probably means a plain or region of Aram. It is commonly identified with the area around Haran in northern Mesopotamia.
The verb “vaye’etar” describes pleading or earnest supplication, not merely making a brief request. It emphasizes Isaac’s persistent prayer for his wife.
In biblical language, “to inquire of the Lord” can mean seeking divine guidance or an answer. It does not simply mean searching or studying.
The prophecy uses paired words such as “nations” and “peoples,” a style known as poetic parallelism. Its statement that the younger will prevail over the older reverses the usual expectation.
The word “tam” does not mean naive or unintelligent here. In the Bible, it can describe someone whole, honest, and even-tempered.
The sequence “he ate, drank, got up, and left” makes the exchange feel rushed. The ending emphasizes that Esau not only felt hungry but also treated his birthright with contempt.
